correctness.rationale: The graph has six vertices with isolated vertices counted in k(A). For each of the 36 distinct unordered pairs, stripping only the marked activities from the four occupation cells gives Cov=x_e x_f(F00 F11-F10 F01)/Z². The separately written integer replay (branches/2760e33c-5e6f-463f-a09b-d3e7f82e1958/k33_independent_replay.py) enumerated all 512 subsets, multiplied each quotient back by q²(1-q), and matched the frozen certificate coefficient by coefficient for every pair. The automorphisms fixing the defect produce eight actual pair orbits, with sizes 4,4,2,4,8,8,4,2. Their distinct quotients have 26,25,65,58,67,64,65,58 monomials, all with positive coefficients on the support. Thus each quotient is strictly positive for positive q,v,w, and the normalized covariance is strictly negative since additionally 1-q>0 and Z>0. This covers all independent choices of q,v,w in the stated domain, including w=v; it does not cover nine independent edge activities, general K_m,n, or negative association. The accompanying replay JSON and summary are in the same replay directory. Frozen verify.py was inspected, not executed.

evidence: Cao–Fu Theorems 1.1–1.2 cover complete bipartite graphs K_m,n with m,n≥2 under the uniform forest and uniform connected-spanning-subgraph measures. Although they include this graph, they do not quantify over positive cluster weight and a freely varying defect activity.

Zhao–Zhou's broader all-edge-weight result requires rank or corank at most three. Tang–Zhang Theorem 1.2 requires a connected regular graph sequence of growing degree, isoperimetry, a pair distance bound, and homogeneous p; it does not specialize to a fixed cubic K3,3 with mixed activities.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The strongest broader statements have genuinely nonmatching parameter, rank or graph assumptions. Stronger graph coverage in a boundary ensemble does not imply the interior finite-q theorem.

evidence: At common unit activity the q↓0 law on a connected graph selects uniform connected spanning subgraphs. Negativity in that boundary law or in a uniform forest law cannot decide sign throughout the positive-q interval or independently for all w>0.

Series–parallel two-sum closure does not imply a statement on K3,3. A one-defect certificate for K5 cannot be specialized by equating or deleting activities to this six-vertex graph. Two fixed-host proofs using similar enumeration do not establish a common general theorem.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The verified result fills the stated interior/fugacity gap without claiming priority for the generic Rayleigh identity, the homogeneous slice on its own, or every bipartite graph.

evidence: Via the multiaffine partition function the covariance sign is the conditional four-cell Rayleigh difference sign; the cycle matroid uses r(A)=6-k(A), so the usual rank and component weights differ only by a fixed power of q under the corresponding multivariate Tutte convention.

The K3,3 cycle matroid has rank 5 and corank 4; exchanging rank and corank by duality does not move it into the ≤3 theorem. The graph has a K4 minor (contract two disjoint opposite-part edges), so the series–parallel route does not apply.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Compared random-cluster, multivariate Tutte and matroid Rayleigh formulations, rather than treating their different names or the planar-bipartite label as novelty. The certificate specializes to a two-activity slice and does not establish an arbitrary-weight matroid property.

originality.rationale: Best of current knowledge for the whole one-defect positive-activity K3,3 family at 0<q<1, not for negative correlation on this host under every measure. The graph falls outside the rank/corank and series–parallel results, and the known complete-bipartite uniform forest and uniform connected-spanning ensembles are different laws. The comparable one-defect K5 record is a different fixed host, not a stronger graph theorem. No historical priority guarantee.
residual_risks: The corpus check was bounded and one forest record was only available via its index. An unpublished or unindexed weighted K3,3 computation or a general theorem beyond the inspected sufficient conditions could overlap. No claim of world priority or of coverage exclusion for unread text.

value.rationale: K3,3 is a natural small non-series-parallel bipartite test case outside the rank/corank cutoff. A single weighted bond models the smallest nonhomogeneous perturbation while allowing arbitrarily strong disorder, not just perturbation of equal weights. All-pair, full-domain sign with integer certificates gives an exact benchmark for when negative dependence persists despite that disorder. The domain-wide conclusion does not follow from a small rational grid or an endpoint ensemble.
